 MORE-SPORTS Marathons Who was Rachel Apa? The young runner who died trying to finish the New York Marathon at age 24
 A new tragedy affects one of the great mass-participation races of international athletics
 Rachel Apa, 24, passed away after collapsing while running the New York City Marathon last Sunday. @rachelapa 
 IVÁN CAMILO&NBSP; CASTIBLANCO

 The recent edition of the New York Marathon was overshadowed by a tragedy that has shocked the world of sports and the international running community. Rachel Apa , a 24-year-old young woman, lost her life after suddenly collapsing when she was just two miles away from crossing the finish line.
 The event, which brought together tens of thousands of athletes on the streets of New York, was marked by this tragic outcome that abruptly cut short the sporting dream of a promising athlete . Marathon authorities and the family have begun to clarify the heartbreaking details of her final hours on the course.
 The sporting event was proceeding normally under the watchful gaze of thousands of spectators who packed the different districts of the city. However, fate had a painful ordeal in store for the young competitor's loved ones .
 The illusion of a sporting debut turned into a nightmare
 Rachel Apa was taking part in her first official marathon with a deep personal and charitable purpose . Months of rigorous training preceded race day, when the athlete was aiming to complete the demanding 42 kilometers of the New York course.
 Her connection to sports went back a long way, standing out for her time as a field hockey player at Bucknell University in Pennsylvania. That solid athletic foundation gave her the confidence to take on the challenge with optimal physical preparedness.
 The  reason behind every kilometer covered
 Beyond competitive performance, Rachel's main motivation lay in honoring her late grandfather . The young woman had joined the Parkinson's Research Foundation champions team to raise funds and medical awareness .
 During her childhood, her grandfather had been her great role model and inspiration for maintaining an active lifestyle . Seeing how the degenerative disease robbed him of his mobility drove Rachel to run every meter carrying his legacy in her memory.
 Family monitoring and the worrying messages along the way
 As she moved along the urban course, her mother stayed close by at various key points on the circuit. In fact, at kilometer 14 in Queens, one of her last smiles on camera was recorded as she waved euphorically .
 Meanwhile, her father followed every development through the competition’s official app from Pennsylvania. Communication via text messages reflected how extreme fatigue began to take a toll on the runner’s body as she passed the halfway mark of the race .
 The warning signs and the tragic collapse in Central Park
 Upon reaching miles 18 and 19, Rachel replied to her father with short, expressive messages such as «Ouch» and «Ow, ow», showing the accumulated physical suffering . Despite the pain, she kept moving forward with admirable determination until communication stopped completely in the final stretches.
 Around mile 24, already deep into the iconic Central Park, the young woman suddenly collapsed onto the asphalt before the astonished gaze of those present . A social worker and several doctors who witnessed the incident immediately ran over to begin cardiopulmonary resuscitation maneuvers.
 The desperate medical attempts to save her life
 The marathon's emergency services quickly deployed an automated defibrillator at the scene in an attempt to stabilize the runner. Minutes later, an ambulance rushed her to Mount Sinai Hospital amid enormous family anguish .
 Her mother managed to reach the scene just as the ambulance was leaving and accompanied her daughter during the trip to the hospital. The medical specialists fought tirelessly for approximately six hours in the emergency area, although unfortunately they could not prevent the fatal outcome .
 The medical diagnosis and the family's overwhelming pain
 Hours later, her father confirmed to outlets such as The New York Times that doctors determined that the cause of death was rhabdomyolysis . It is a serious muscle condition caused by extreme exertion, in which damaged tissues break down, releasing toxic substances into the bloodstream .
 The news has left an irreparable void among those closest to her and in the event’s organization, which issued statements of condolence. Rachel Apa’s loss transforms her brave attempt into a painful reminder of the physical limits to which the human body is sometimes subjected in ultradistance endurance events .
